article.title: 完形填空 · 别把别人的行为都理解成针对自己
article.context: 文章讨论“个人化解读”和“读心”两种常见认知倾向：人们容易把他人的批评、取消约会等行为解释为对自己的负面评价；更好的做法是挑战这种假设，并尝试从他人的处境寻找替代解释。
rows: Most of us strive for self-respect—to see ourselves in a positive light, to be proud of who we are.
我们大多数人都追求自尊——希望以积极的眼光看待自己，并为真实的自己感到自豪。
advance
Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it's only natural to want to avoid them.
任何削弱这种自我价值感的评论或经历都会令人不舒服，而想要避开它们也是很自然的。
explain
But the thing is, whether your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective.
但问题在于，你的自我价值是否真的受到了损害，在很大程度上是主观的。
contrast
Much of it comes down to your perception of what someone said or did.
这很大程度上取决于你对别人言行的理解。
explain
When you take things personally, you're interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person.
当你把事情往自己身上揽时，你是在把这些情境理解为：它们揭示了关于你这个人的某种重要而负面的东西。
explain
Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you're a poor member of staff.
比如老板挑出了你销售报告中的问题，你离开时却觉得，这意味着她认为你是个表现很差的员工。
example
Or, two of your friends cancel your planned get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they're bored of you.
又或者，两位朋友取消了原本计划好的酒吧聚会，而你把这理解成他们已经厌烦了你。
example
Psychologists have a term for this way of thinking: personalisation.
心理学家给这种思维方式起了一个术语：个人化解读。
emphasize
But the reality is that your boss might view you very highly.
但现实可能是，你的老板其实非常看重你。
contrast
It's just you made Some mistakes in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time.
只不过你在报告中犯了一些错误，她希望把这些问题指出来，好让你下次做得更好。
explain
Similarly, in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just changed their minds.
同样地，就朋友取消聚会而言，也许那周末他们两个人都身体不适，或者只是改变了主意。
compare
In both examples—and others that we all experience—there's another process at work that psychologists call mind reading.
在这两个例子以及我们都会经历的其他情形中，还有另一种心理过程在起作用，心理学家称之为“读心”。
advance
This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you; when you can’t really know without asking them directly.
所谓“读心”，就是你自以为知道别人怎么看你；可如果不直接去问他们，你其实无法真正知道。
explain
One simple way to avoid engaging in personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what's happened.
避免陷入个人化解读和“读心”的一个简单办法，是质疑自己对已经发生之事所作的负面假设。
encourage
When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you—especially in the sense of saying anything deep or fundamental about you.
当你发现自己把某种情境理解成针对个人时，试着寻找一些不那么以自己为中心的解释——尤其不要把它看成在说明关于你本人的什么深层或根本问题。
encourage
When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people's shoes.
这样做时，试着设身处地站在别人角度思考，可能会有所帮助。
encourage
The fact your boss took the time to give you feedback at all means they care enough to want to help you improve.
老板愿意花时间给你反馈，本身就说明她足够在意，愿意帮助你改进。
explain
When it comes to your friends—maybe it's because your friendship is so strong that they felt able to cancel at late notice.
至于你的朋友，也许恰恰因为你们的友谊足够牢固，他们才觉得临时取消也不会伤害这段关系。
conclude
